passage:
Sunday night
First real fight with Adil. Not a sulky one, a real one.
It was about his parents. He'd told them we'd come for lunch every Sunday "from now on", without asking me. I said I also need Sundays for my own family and, honestly, for sleep. He said, "But that's how it's always been in our house." I said, "It's not only your house any more."
He went quiet and walked to the window. I thought, here we go, the silent treatment. But after a few minutes he came back and said, "You're right that I should have asked. I'm upset, but I'm not going anywhere. Can we work out a schedule?"
I'd braced for him to storm off. Instead he stayed in the room while being angry. Nandini always says the first fight tells you more than the first date. I think she's right.
Farida

qa.q: What had Adil told his parents without asking?
qa.a: Adil had told them they'd come for lunch every Sunday 'from now on'.

qa.q: What did Farida expect when Adil walked to the window, and how did that change?
qa.a: Farida braced for the silent treatment, then felt reassured when Adil came back, admitted he should have asked and stayed in the conversation.

qa.q: What did Adil's response show that matters for the future?
qa.a: He could be upset and still stay, own his part and move to problem-solving, which suggests they can handle later disagreements together.

qa.q: How might Adil's parents experience the new schedule talk?
qa.a: Adil's parents may feel disappointed at fewer Sunday lunches, since weekly lunches are how it has always been in their house.

grounding: Shows a couple's first real disagreement over time with parents, where how each behaves reveals more about the future than the early months.

Salma: you said two weeks in Dubai. the email says six
Kiran: it just got extended today. I was going to tell you tonight
Salma: my cousin's nikah is on the 14th. you promised
Kiran: I know. I'm sorry. it's a big client, I can't say no in my first year
Salma: you can't say no to them but you can to me?
Kiran: that's not fair
Salma: it's how it feels
Kiran: ok. can I call? I don't want to do this over text
Kiran: I don't want to be the boyfriend who always picks work. but I also need this job
Salma: and I need to know where I fit
Kiran: you fit first. we need a way to decide travel together, not me just announcing it
Salma: ok. call me at 9. I'm still upset 😔
Kiran: I know. I'll call at 9 🙏

What does Salma mean by 'I need to know where I fit'?
qa.a: Salma worries that work will always come before the relationship and wants to feel like a priority in Kiran's decisions.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Kiran and Salma here?
qa.a: They can move the argument to a call and agree on a way to decide travel together, instead of Kiran announcing plans after the fact.

qa.a: Kiran feels torn between a big client in his first year and his promise to Salma, and doesn't want to be someone who always picks work.
